topicName: VNet Peering, VPN Gateway, and ExpressRoute
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Enterprise Networking in Azure: VNet Peering, VPN Gateway, and ExpressRoute"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Designing a robust cloud architecture in Microsoft Azure requires a deep understanding of connectivity options. As workloads scale, isolated Virtual Networks (VNets) need to communicate securely with each other and with on-premises environments. This tutorial covers the implementation and architectural differences between VNet Peering, VPN Gateway, and Azure ExpressRoute."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"1. Azure VNet Peering"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"VNet Peering enables you to seamlessly connect two or more Virtual Networks in Azure. Once peered, the VNets appear as one for connectivity purposes. Traffic between virtual machines in peered VNets uses the Microsoft backbone network; traffic is routed through the private IP addresses only, without public internet exposure."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Characteristics of VNet Peering"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Low-latency, high-bandwidth connection across VNets."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Support for inter-region peering (Global VNet Peering)."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"No downtime to resources when creating the peering."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"az network vnet peering create --name \"VNet1ToVNet2\" --g \"MyResourceGroup\" --vnet-name \"VNet1\" --remote-vnet \"/subscriptions/{SubID}/resourceGroups/MyResourceGroup/providers/Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/VNet2\" --allow-vnet-access"},{"order":10,"type":"heading","text":"2. Azure VPN Gateway"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"An Azure VPN Gateway is a specific type of virtual network gateway that sends encrypted traffic between your Azure virtual network and your on-premises location over the public internet. You can also use a VPN Gateway to send traffic between Azure VNets (VNet-to-VNet)."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Gateway Types and Configurations"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"PolicyBased: Uses static routing tables with IPsec policies specified."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"RouteBased: Uses dynamic routing protocols (BGP) to select routes based on packet destination."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"az network vnet-gateway create --name \"MyVpnGateway\" --resource-group \"MyResourceGroup\" --vnet \"MyVNet\" --public-ip-address \"MyVpnPublicIP\" --gateway-type Vpn --vpn-type RouteBased --sku VpnGw1 --no-wait"},{"order":16,"type":"heading","text":"3. Azure ExpressRoute"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"ExpressRoute lets you create private connections between Azure datacenters and infrastructure on your premises or in a colocation environment. ExpressRoute connections do not go over the public internet, and offer higher security, reliability, and lower latencies than typical VPN connections."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"ExpressRoute Routing Domains (Peerings)"},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Azure Private Peering: Connectivity to services deployed on IaaS and PaaS (Virtual Networks)."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Microsoft Peering: Connectivity to Microsoft 365 and public PaaS services."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"az network express-route create --name \"MyExpressRouteCircuit\" --resource-group \"MyResourceGroup\" --peering-location \"Silicon Valley\" --bandwidth 1000 --provider \"Equinix\" --sku-family MeteredData --sku-tier Enterprise"},{"order":22,"type":"heading","text":"Summary Comparison"},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"VNet Peering: Best for cloud-to-cloud (Azure-to-Azure) internal networking."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"VPN Gateway: Best for cost-effective, encrypted site-to-site connectivity over the public internet."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ExpressRoute: Best for mission-critical, high-throughput, low-latency, and secure enterprise connectivity."}]
